record.paper_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
record.original_question: What security mechanisms can provide integrity and authentication, not only confidentiality, for underwater wireless optical communication systems, given that the surveyed literature mainly studies confidentiality and only a few theoretical works study quantum key distribution for direct light-based air-water communication?

evidence.quote: In underwater wireless optical communication, the literature does not contain contributions on integrity and authentication (except few theoretical works, which studied only QKD in direct light air-water wireless communication); instead, the literature seems to be mainly focusing on confidentiality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) system in which one or more transmitters send information-bearing optical signals (e.g., via LEDs or laser diodes) through a water channel — possibly crossing the air–water interface — to one or more receivers (e.g., photodetectors). The channel is affected by absorption, scattering, turbulence, and link misalignment, and may be subject to passive eavesdropping as well as active adversaries who can inject, modify, replay, or impersonate optical signals.

Three standard security goals are considered:
(i) Confidentiality: an unauthorized receiver cannot recover the transmitted message.
(ii) Integrity: any unauthorized modification of a transmitted message between legitimate transmitter and receiver is detectable.
(iii) Authentication: a legitimate receiver can verify that received messages originate from a claimed legitimate transmitter (and not from an impersonator).

Design and rigorously analyze cryptographic and/or physical-layer security mechanisms for UWOC (including air–water optical links) that simultaneously provide integrity and authentication — beyond confidentiality alone — and that are practical under the bandwidth, latency, energy, and channel-impairment constraints typical of underwater optical links. In particular, develop schemes for such links (other than quantum key distribution for direct air–water optical communication) that achieve provable integrity and entity/message authentication, and characterize their achievable security guarantees and performance trade-offs.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns an open research direction in underwater wireless optical communication security. Available surveys note a gap in integrity and authentication mechanisms for UWOC, with most physical-layer-security work focused on confidentiality and only limited theoretical QKD studies for air–water links. No comprehensive solution providing provable integrity and authentication tailored to UWOC has been established in the literature to date.

status_evidence.title: Physical layer security in underwater wireless optical communication (survey context)
status_evidence.snippet: Literature on UWOC mainly addresses confidentiality; integrity and authentication are largely unaddressed except for limited QKD studies in air-water optical links.
status_evidence.claim: Integrity and authentication mechanisms for UWOC remain an open problem.
